From 1925 to 1947, the nighttime waters of Maryland were more navigable thanks to lighthouse keepers Fannie May Salter and Ida Lewis.
Before automation, lighthouse keepers like Fannie May Salter, who served for twenty-two years, and Ida Lewis were crucial to ensuring safe navigation for watercraft.
Fannie May Salter worked as a lighthouse keeper for twenty-two years, but Ida Lewis did so for even longer: fifty-four years.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- An isthmus is a strip of land that connects two larger pieces of land across an expanse of water.
- It is also known as a land bridge.
- The Isthmus of Ierapetra connects the Siteia municipality to the rest of the island of Crete.
- The Isthmus of Ierapetra is located in the Mediterranean Sea.

The student wants to indicate the location of the Isthmus of Ierapetra.
questions.question: The student wants to indicate the location of the Isthmus of Ierapetra. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: An isthmus, or land bridge, like the Isthmus of Ierapetra, connects two larger pieces of land.
An isthmus, also known as a land bridge, is a strip of land that connects two larger pieces of land across an expanse of water.
One example of an isthmus is the Isthmus of Ierapetra.
The Isthmus of Ierapetra is located in the Mediterranean Sea, where it connects the Siteia municipality to the rest of the island of Crete.
